builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DAQ: Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Transformers
summary: DAQ replaces standard post-training quantization of spiking transformers with a decision-aligned calibration that keeps quantized membrane variables inside the floating-point model's firing regions along the quantized model's own trajectory. It requires only calibration data and no retraining, enabling 4-bit weights and membrane variables, but adds a state-trajectory-dependent calibration procedure more complex than generic PTQ. It can fail when firing decisions near decision boundaries diverge over recurrent time steps, and its energy benefits depend on spiking or neuromorphic deployment targets rather than conventional GPU inference.
rationale: DAQ is a PTQ calibration method specific to spiking transformers and event-based workloads, which are outside the typical LLM/VLM production stack of a constrained-infrastructure ML engineer, so it is relevant to track but not to adopt unless the team deploys spiking neural networks.

claims.statement: DAQ replaces standard post-training quantization of spiking transformers with a decision-aligned calibration that keeps quantized membrane variables inside the floating-point model's firing regions along the quantized model's own trajectory. It requires only calibration data and no retraining, enabling 4-bit weights and membrane variables, but adds a state-trajectory-dependent calibration procedure more complex than generic PTQ. It can fail when firing decisions near decision boundaries diverge over recurrent time steps, and its energy benefits depend on spiking or neuromorphic deployment targets rather than conventional GPU inference.
On FE108 with SDTrack, DAQ achieves 58.8% AUC and 90.9% PR with 4-bit weights and membrane variables while reducing energy by 66.2% versus the unquantized baseline.
